transcript.text: micrwave keeps tripping the eletric, not every time but like 1 in 3 when i press start, whole kitchen goes off. had to reset the fuse box 4 times today

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Stop using the microwave and leave it unplugged. A microwave that trips the kitchen circuit intermittently when Start is pressed needs a qualified appliance engineer; do not keep resetting the breaker and retrying it. The most likely causes are a failing door interlock/monitor switch or latch alignment, which can fault as the programme starts, or a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit. A damaged lead, plug or socket is less likely but still needs ruling out. Microwave internals can retain dangerous stored electrical charge even when unplugged, so do not remove its casing or attempt an internal fuse/part repair. With it unplugged only:
1. Check the plug, lead and visible socket area for scorching, melting, looseness or damage. If any is present, do not use the socket until it has been checked.
2. Check that the door closes cleanly and feels firm, with no broken-looking plastic hooks, food debris in the latch slots, or obvious sagging. This can point towards the door-latch/interlock route. An engineer should test the interlocks and high-voltage circuit safely. The timing of the trip—instantly at Start versus just as heating begins—will help them distinguish the likely fault.

ok il leave it unplugged. plug and lead look ok, no burn marks. door sometimes needs a push to shut and theres a bit of crusty food round the catches. it also gives a loud bang from inside sometimes when it trips

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The door needing an extra push, plus food around the catches, makes a misaligned latch and door interlock/monitor switch the leading cause. Those switches can trip the circuit if they operate in the wrong sequence. However, a loud bang from inside means an internal high-voltage fault or arcing also has to be ruled out. That is not a normal microwave noise and reinforces that it needs a qualified microwave appliance engineer, not further test runs. Cleaning the accessible food debris may be worthwhile, but it does not prove the microwave is safe or remove the need for repair. With it unplugged only, inspect the cavity for the signs in the question above. A burnt or holed waveguide cover, scorch mark or damaged paint would point to arcing; if it all looks undamaged, the door latch/interlock route becomes still more likely. Do not remove the casing or attempt to test or bypass any door switches.
